subject: MedIntel MAP: hosting acceptance criteria & timeline
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@medintel.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedIntel MAP: hosting acceptance criteria & timeline

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a draft MAP that splits evaluation checkpoints across three lanes: Hosted (fast onramp), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on‑prem). Key asks for you to confirm:

- Which deployment lanes are needed for go/no‑go at pilot (Week 6)?
- Acceptance criteria we should lock for the MAP (latency P95, throughput, data isolation).
- Procurement timing for contract & SOC2 evidence (Procurement team CC'd).

High level proposal (summary in attachment):
- Week 0–2: POC on Hosted with sandbox data (validate latency and inference correctness).
- Week 3–4: Dedicated run to validate sustained throughput with MedIntel test suite.
- Week 5–6: Private (VPC) gating for PHI workloads — security proofing + audit.

Attachments: [MedIntel_MAP_v5.xlsx (xlsx)], [SOC2_snapshot.pdf (pdf)]

If you can confirm which lane you want to prioritize we’ll lock the MAP and send a DocuSign for the contract addendum. Proposed milestone dates are included in the spreadsheet.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@medintel.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: MedIntel Procurement <procurement@medintel.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MedIntel MAP: hosting acceptance criteria & timeline

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear summary and the MAP. A few quick responses from our side:

- For pilot we need Hosted for user acceptance testing but only with non‑PHI synthetic data.
- Goal is to have Dedicated by ramp (production) if performance delta is material; otherwise we may keep Hosted with committed capacity.
- Private/VPC is required for the regulated PHI path — that lane must be fully audited before PHI can move.

Procurement: what SOC2 artifacts can Redwood provide this week? Procurement will need a versioned SOC2 snapshot and a data processing addendum.

Also: can you add a clear rollback/fallback plan in the MAP if latency regressions occur during Week 3 load tests?

Cc'ing procurement to start paperwork.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of AI Platform, MedIntel
alyssa@medintel.com

Subject: Re: MedIntel MAP: hosting acceptance criteria & timeline

Alyssa / Rachel —

Appreciate the clarity, Alyssa. Quick proposal to balance speed and compliance:

- Phase A (Week 0–4): Hosted sandbox for UAT with synthetic data. Acceptance: P95 latency < 250ms for 8k token average prompt; token accuracy within tolerance on our eval set.
- Phase B (Week 3–6 overlap option): Dedicated reserved queue for sustained throughput tests (500 rps sustained for 30m). Acceptance: throughput validated, cost runbook accepted.
- Phase C (Week 5–8): Private/VPC cutover for PHI — gated by SOC2 evidence + VPC runbook review.

Fallbacks / rollback: if latency > 350ms during load (Week 3 test), automatic fallback to smaller model variant + circuit breaker alerting to MedIntel oncall. We can include an A/B canary and a 24‑hour freeze window for change control.

If that sequencing works, Rachel and I will update the MAP (timeline and acceptance matrix) and submit a DocuSign exhibit for the reserved capacity amendment.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Alyssa —

Quick technical notes to support the MAP:

- Private/VPC: we can deliver a customer‑managed VPC peering model. Expect a 2–3 week prep window for firewall rules, shared subnets, and KMS integration once the runbook is accepted.
- Data residency: for PHI we recommend provisioning Dedicated nodes in the same AWS region (us‑west‑2) while the VPC gating completes.
- Runbook: attaching a short VPC_runbook_draft.pdf (stub) with checklist items (routing, certs, test harness).

I'll be available during the Week 3 load run to help tune batching and KV cache parameters. If you want, Laura and I can lead a 60‑minute runbook walkthrough with your infra team before Week 5.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Solutions, Redwood Inference
